title: The features super funds are seeking from candidates
full_text:
Specialist recruiter Kaizen has shared the features that superannuation funds are seeking from candidates as multiple funds seek senior hires.
In recent months, several super funds such as HESTA, Equip, First Super, Legalsuper and GESB have been seeking new chief executives or other senior roles such as chief investment officers.
From its experience, specialist financial services recruiter Kaizen said there are seven features that funds are seeking from their candidates.
These are:
- Member-first thinking
- No-ego mindset
- Cultural alignment
- Team orientation
- Adaptability
- Accountability
- Long-term commitment
It also stated that ‘salary alone is rarely the deciding factor’ as candidates consider factors such as professional development, career progression, flexible work and strong employer brands. Beyond the role itself, candidates are considering how a fund invests in its people and their opportunities for long-term career growth.
This means funds should consider their employee value proposition and how they compare to rival funds.
Paris Deligianis, senior recruiter at Kaizen, said: “The talent challenge facing superannuation funds is no longer solely about adviser numbers. Success increasingly depends on how effectively organisations understand, attract, develop and retain people in a highly competitive market.
“The funds achieving the strongest hiring outcomes are those that understand both sides of the equation, recognise what candidates value, clearly communicate their expectations, and provide an environment where both can align.”
Earlier this year, Claire Tate, managing director of financial services recruitment firm Keegan Adams, said the leadership roles in superannuation have changed dramatically from their previous responsibilities.
This level of pressure is in place regardless of fund size- at the largest funds, they are exposed to public scrutiny with complex internal frameworks while smaller funds are navigating the same regulatory and technology landscape but working with far smaller and limited budgets.
Speaking to Super Review, she said: “C-suite roles have undergone dramatic transformation. Previously, a CIO or COO could be heavily focused on investment or operations. Today they have half a dozen priorities to address all at once. They must simultaneously navigate regulatory scrutiny, tech transformation, cybersecurity, retirement solutions strategy and member expectations, and have the deep experience and know-how to balance and succeed at every one.
“Meanwhile boards are demanding that leaders build and retain teams for the next phase of the industry – in a market where talent is tight. The pressure is immense. And at smaller funds these huge pressures are on the team to deliver with minimal resources.”
author: Laura Dew
